channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [6] Altermagnetism in a new light
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Zhaoju Yang

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Photonic crystal analog of altermagnetism exploring symmetry-driven spin-split bands related to user interest.

Tags: #altermagnetism #photonics #symmetry

Abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. A photonic crystal now reproduces this symmetry-driven phenomenon using circular polarization as a spin analogue.

item.title: [8] Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Jörg Schmalian, B. J. Ramshaw

Authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important phase diagram study of the candidate topological superconductor UTe2.

Tags: #UTe2 #superconductivity #topology

Abstract: The candidate topological superconductor UTe2 exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. In particular, the apparent observation of two intersecting second-order phase boundaries at a triple point in the pressureâtemperature phase diagram is thermodynamically forbidden. This suggests either a hidden phase transition or a fundamental misunderstanding of the superconductivity in this material. Here we observe an additional phase boundary that is characterized by an upward jump in the sound velocity. This is direct thermodynamic evidence for a phase transition in which superconducting order is lost on cooling. Our results establish a tetracritical point beyond which the ambient and pressure-induced superconducting order parameters form a multicomponent state. We use the measured phase diagram to demonstrate that strong competition between the two superconducting order parameters drives the loss of order when cooling, and leads to phase locking that suppresses superconducting fluctuations. These findings provide the definitive magnetic fieldâpressureâtemperature phase diagram of UTe2 and establish a thermodynamic foundation for multicomponent superconductivity.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Kin Fai Mak, Xiaomeng Liu

Authors: Jinghao Deng, Jiabin Xie, Hongyuan Li, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Explores superconductivity, multiferroicity, and Berry curvature in multilayer graphene with flat bands.

Tags: #transport #graphene #superconductivity #Berry-curvature

Abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene has become a platform for exploring correlated and topological quantum phases, enabled by its flat bands that carry Berry curvature. However, previous studies have mainly focused on separated conduction and valence bands. Here we study the semimetallic regime of rhombohedral hexalayer graphene in which the conduction and valence bands overlap. We reveal a rich phase diagram dominated by flavour-symmetry breaking, featuring correlated insulators, several pockets of superconductivity and two distinct multiferroic orbital magnetic orders. Near a band inversion, we observe two superconducting-like states confined to regions with coexisting electron and hole Fermi surfaces, suggesting a possible dual-carrier origin. Additionally, we identify a ferroelectric orbital magnetic state that undergoes sharp switching under unipolar electric fields, which signals spontaneous electric polarization. Unlike previously reported multiferroicity near zero electric field, this state exhibits magnetic hysteresis reversible by electric field, consistent with a phenomenological model of coupled electric and magnetic polarization. Our work elucidates the correlated semimetal regime in rhombohedral graphene and underscores its potential to host diverse quantum phases.

item.title: [10] Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
item.description:
Last authors: A. J. Millis, F. Boschini

Authors: D. Armanno, O. Gingras, F. Goto, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct tr-ARPES study of competing pseudogap and superconducting states in optimally doped cuprates.

Tags: #tr-ARPES #cuprates #superconductivity #pseudogap

Abstract: High-temperature cuprate superconductors remain a key platform for studying the competition and coexistence of emergent quantum phases of matter. These include non-s-wave superconductivity with a high transition temperature, non-Fermi-liquid transport and the pseudogap regime. How superconductivity emerges alongside and competes with the pseudogap remains an open question. Here, by directly accessing the near-antinodal region of optimally doped Bi-based cuprates via time- and angle-resolved photoemission, we report a transient change from a symmetric superconducting-like density of states to an asymmetric pseudogap-like density of states when superconductivity is disrupted by a sufficiently high excitation fluence. We observe this change at electronic temperatures well below the equilibrium superconducting critical temperature. Conversely, when superconductivity is fully restored, the pseudogap is suppressed, as indicated by a particleâhole-symmetric density of states. We also observe the coexistence of pseudogap and superconducting features at intermediate times or intermediate fluence. Our findings challenge the view that superconductivity emerges from phase coherence in the pseudogap. Instead, we show that the two states compete and that the low-temperature ground state of cuprates reflects an interplay between the superconducting and pseudogap states.

item.title: [8] Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
item.description:
Last authors: K. Jin, N. E. Hussey

Authors: C. M. Duffy, S. J. Tu, Q. H. Chen, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetotransport study identifying antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations as the pairing glue in electron-doped cuprates.

Tags: #transport #cuprates #superconductivity #spin-fluctuations

Abstract: In conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors, the transition temperature and the linear-in-temperature normal-state scattering rate are linked through the electron–phonon coupling strength. In cuprate high-temperature superconductors, no equivalent relationship between critical temperature and electron–boson coupling has been identified. Here we highlight such a link with electrons scattering off commensurate antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations of variable strength. We use d.c. resistivity and high-field magnetoresistance to extract the scattering rate in electron-doped La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 as a function of doping. We reveal a highly anisotropic inelastic component to the scattering rate whose magnitude diminishes markedly as doping increases. The correlation we highlight between the strength of scattering and the critical temperature then identifies low-energy spin fluctuations as the primary pairing glue in electron-doped cuprates. The contrasting magnetotransport behaviour in hole-doped cuprates suggests that the higher critical temperature in those materials cannot be attributed solely to an increase in the coupling strength to the antiferromagnetic fluctuations. The success in modelling La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 reinforces the notion that resolving the origin of high-temperature superconductivity in hole-doped cuprates may require more than a simple extension of the Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer theory.

item.title: [8] Rich quantum phase diagram revealed in semimetallic rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Correlated states, band inversion, and superconductivity in a few-layer graphene system.

Tags: #experiment #rhombohedralgraphene #superconductivity

Abstract: Previous studies of rhombohedral graphene have focused on a single topological and flat conduction or valence band isolated by strong electric fields. Rhombohedral hexalayer graphene is now found to host various quantum phenomena in the correlated semimetallic regime, featuring symmetry breaking, electric-field-driven band inversion, dual-carrier superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism.
